plain.core: Irrep surface codes are two-dimensional topological codes built so that a chosen finite group of logical gates is transversal. The gates must be finite, as the Eastin-Knill theorem requires up to phases, and irreducible. Diagonal finite groups and reversible classical gates can be embedded. Lattice surgery is given to move information between these codes and ordinary surface codes when one of two sufficient conditions holds.
plain.why: E-QEC is the surface-code layer. A code tailored to a gate group is still that layer. No device result, so C4 stays.
plain.limit: Bare arXiv. A design and a surgery condition, not a processor.

plain.why: Corrects the Layer 3 alpha-energy premise: 8.7 MeV is shared by three alphas, so no single alpha carries '2.9 to 8.7 MeV'. The alpha spectrum is the input for any phase-space repopulation or direct-conversion term.
plain.limit: Diagnostics review with channel energies from kinematics, not a new nuclear-data measurement. Laser-driven, not a thermal burn. 91.8 keV is the 8Be ground-state decay Q, not the primary fusion Q. Moves no C. No version bump.

cards.math: A finite-width Majorana shutter as a time-dependent scattering defect. The zero-frequency scattering matrix of a smooth shutter is fixed by the integrated coupling. cards.math: For a stationary gyrotropic equilibrium the kinetic susceptibility is said to obey chi(omega*, k) = R chi(omega, k)* R with R = diag(1, -1, 1). The linearized Vlasov-Maxwell Hamiltonian is said to be PT-symmetric, and the same claim is made for homogeneous Vlasov-Poisson. Instabilities of nonmonotonic, ring, loss-cone, and energetic-particle distributions are identified with spontaneous PT breaking through Krein collisions. Definite-sign cyclotron residues are said to protect thermal Bernstein modes. An analytical threshold and growth rate are claimed for the Dory-Guest-Harris distribution, but the abstract does not print them, so they are not entered. Author Hong Qin. arXiv:2610.03433v1, submitted 2026-10-02, physics.plasm-ph.

plain.core: Layer codes are three-dimensional local CSS codes with check weight at most six, made by quasi-concatenating an input code with surface-code patches. This paper builds the syndrome circuits, including the junctions a borrowed surface-code schedule cannot handle, and compares eighteen of them with surface codes of the same distance under circuit-level noise.
plain.why: E-QEC is where a memory either holds or it does not. The [[4,2,2]] family reaches a simulated circuit-level threshold of 5.06(7)e-3 and idles longer than a rotated surface code of the same distance, at the cost of more operations and about five times as many physical qubits per logical qubit. That is a simulation, not a below-threshold hardware run. C stays at C4. Importance 88 is still a harvest gauge.
plain.limit: Bare arXiv. The threshold and the idle-time factors are circuit simulations at fixed distance, not a device, and not a license to scale one parameter without bound. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80.

cards.math: Decoder-free scheduler: constrain hook propagation, then compress depth. Eighteen layer-code circuits across four input codes, simulated and decoded like surface codes of the same distance. Hook errors do not cut distance on [[4,2,2]]-input codes where a circuit-distance proof fits, and those circuits beat a general-purpose CSS scheduler at about half the CNOT depth per round. Primary [[4,2,2]] family: circuit-level threshold 5.06(7) x 10^-3. At equal distance the layer code tolerates 1.7-3.0 times longer idle between rounds than the rotated surface code, at 1.7-5.0 times more operations per unit time and about five times more physical qubits per logical qubit. Beyond-2D cross-plane CNOT speed matters more than fidelity in their cost model. 22 pages. arXiv:2609.39522, submitted 2026-09-30.

plain.core: The toric code can be thought of as a symmetry that is not a simple on-site spin flip, because its excitations are anyons. The paper proves that no finite extra quantum system can turn that symmetry into an on-site one. Infinite-dimensional extras can, but only if their energy is not bounded from below.

plain.core: Abelian anyons in a fractional quantum Hall fluid pick up a phase when they trade places. The paper designs a small interferometer where an open quantum dot makes that swap show up as a shift between two interference patterns, and writes a formula for the current at finite temperature.
plain.why: Measurement is already required to read anyons. The proposal is a cousin of that fact. It is not the primitive we load.

Two-drain subtraction avoids the area-screening assumption, with a stated few-percent systematic error.

Which plaquette carries which Abelian anyon depends on the couplings. Adding Heisenberg exchange produces ordinary magnetic order.
plain.why: The Majorana mapping is real Kitaev physics. The phase they find is the Abelian code we already do not use as the universal primitive. S3 remains the braid path.

plain.core: A new family of quantum error-correcting codes is built by twisting a classical expander code with a non-Abelian D4 gauge theory. plain.core: A fusion plant may want a thin edge plasma so ion-cyclotron antennas do not sputter the wall. WEST has already run that way with little impurity. The usual cold-plasma formula then predicts infinite radiofrequency electric fields. Collisions make the peaks finite but only micrometers wide, which a 2D finite-element mesh can resolve. Those peaks are still as sharp as the hot-plasma physics the cold model left out.
plain.why: E-RL's actuators include radiofrequency heating. A controller that trusts a cold-plasma antenna model in the low-density edge will be aiming at a singularity. This is a warning for Bus A, not a closed control loop, so M2 stays open.
plain.limit: No coil command, no latency budget, no disruption-rate comparison with DIII-D, TCV, or WEST's own controller. Micrometer scales are not a P_drive entry.

plain.core: Full gyrokinetic turbulence is too slow to sit inside a pulse planner, so people use a quasilinear shortcut closed by a saturation rule. PQLS is that shortcut in general geometry, electromagnetic and collisional, and it matches GENE growth rates. The saturation rule (SAT3) is fitted to published nonlinear CGYRO cases with a Bayesian split between coefficient error and model-form error, and the resulting profiles track the full simulation.
plain.why: S-L3 says keep the kinetic solvers in the rate. A differentiable quasilinear solver with an honest uncertainty on its closure is a methods result on that shelf. It does not compute a driven-barrier reactivity, and it does not write a plant Q.
plain.limit: The closure is still a fit. Zonal flows and avalanches can leave the quasilinear picture. No hole-burning, no SRS/SBS, no P_fusion. Bare arXiv.

plain.core: Short quantum-dot Kitaev chains host poor-man's Majorana modes whose spin was usually ignored. The authors couple that parity qubit to an ordinary spin qubit. They then show, in the model, universal control of the parity qubit, a readout, and an entangling gate.
plain.why: E-MZM is on watch until M5. A gate set on poor-man's modes shows the mimic platform can look like a qubit. It does not show a topological gap that grows with wire length, and it does not supply independent X and Z logicals.
plain.limit: Effective model of a minimal Kitaev chain. Poor-man's end modes are the mimic class (Andreev substitutes included). Does not move C1. Not load-bearing.

plain.core: A way to build quantum error-correcting codes from non-Abelian sheaves so the code stays sparse, keeps a constant fraction of its qubits as logical qubits, and still catches small errors. Gauging those codes can also prepare a magic state inside the code.
plain.why: This sits on E-QEC, the error layer Bus B already uses. It is the same shelf as qLDPC, not a new bus and not an S3 braid. It does not replace the surface-code hardware that earned C4.
plain.limit: Bare arXiv existence proof. No decoder on a device, no threshold number that tightens the ledger, and no fusion measurement. Cannot raise C and does not pass Auto-Gate.

cards.math: Cup-product gauging of sheaf codes; Knill–Laflamme distance; expansion plus cleaning. Assumes a family with constant rate and linear distance, and that gauging preserves the logical constraints they solve by explicit representatives.

plain.core: After the usual resonant error-field coils have done their job, leftover non-resonant fields can still hurt a tokamak. This recipe picks coil currents that keep both the resonant response and the neoclassical torque small, and it tries that recipe on ITER target plasmas.
plain.why: Bus A (E-RL) has to live with error-field coils. A torque-aware correction is a candidate actuator map for ITER-class machines. It is not a closed control loop and it does not beat a lab disruption baseline, so M2 stays open.
plain.limit: Scenario calculation, not a shot. No latency budget, no safe-hold, no stored-energy flattop versus DIII-D or TCV. Bare arXiv cannot raise E-RL.

plain.core: In a honeycomb model of a pair-density-wave superconductor, half-quantum vortices can be the cheaper defect near a phase transition. Those half-vortices bind Majorana zero modes and, in a magnetic field, arrange into a lattice whose hybridization makes Dirac nodes and zero-energy lines.

plain.core: A tuned extension of the Kitaev honeycomb model in which the flux pattern decides where Majorana fermions are allowed to hop. Their zero-point energy then selects a crystal of visons whose ground space is exactly a toric code.

plain.limit: Exists only at a special loop point of a spin model. A generic perturbation is not shown to protect the degeneracy the way a surface code on hardware does.
